![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130823/assets/e0fe5ad37bd641a7d88eb75629f243d383f392230b86be723556d63cedbd8f95.png)

A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the half-ellipses $y=\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}$ and $y=\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}},$ and the lines $x=\pm 1.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $x=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}\le y\le \sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130823/assets/8ac2ade388bcc0dee28b1a5bbaf0807ae253c0c785b9a63978014e873fe8a1ce.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k|y|=ky,$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}ky\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{-1}^{1}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(9-3{x}^{2}-(3-{x}^{2}))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{k}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(6-2{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{-1}^{1}(3-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[3x-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{16k}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=ky=\frac{3}{16}My.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}\frac{3}{16}My|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}\frac{3}{16}My(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}y(x-1)^{2}{\int }_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}(x-1)^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{\sqrt{3-{x}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-3{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}(x-1)^{2}(3-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-6x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M{[-\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{2{x}^{3}}{3}-3{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M(-\frac{2}{5}+0+\frac{4}{3}-0+6) \\  & =\frac{3}{16}M\cdot \frac{104}{15} \\  & =\frac{13M}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
